ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against FINTRAC, OFAC, UN, EU, and Canadian Sanctions lists for PEPs, senior foreign officials, and designated entities

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File administrative appeal with the Registre des entreprises du Québec within 30 days of rejection, providing revised name and supporting documentation for reconsideration

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for non-regulated entities provided physical address for service of process and compliance with Quebec commercial substance rules
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk of unannounced on-site inspections for standard corporate formations

Consular legalization if required for foreign documents

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Federal incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss 7, 19(1), 115(1) and 122; extra-provincial registration and ongoing legality in Quebec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, RLRQ c P-44.1, ss 2, 9 and 25; Quebec-equivalent corporate governance recognized under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, RLRQ c S-31.1, s 3.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) and Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Government of Quebec)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001) under CBCA; Quebec registration application / enterprise register filing (application for registration of a legal person) under RLRQ c P-44.1
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the CBCA or QBCA; authorized capital may be ordinary shares without par value and initial paid-up capital may be nominal. No escrow deposit or capital-blocking account is required for incorporation; however, the Quebec private-employment-agency permit regime may require a financial guarantee or surety bond as a licensing condition.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. The subscription of 100 common shares without par value for aggregate consideration of CAD 100.00 is approved and issued as fully paid. 2. The registered office in the Province of Quebec, at [address], is adopted as the corporation's registered office and records office. 3. [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] is appointed Corporate Secretary, to serve until successors are appointed. 4. Management is authorized to open bank accounts, execute tax and payroll registrations, and take all necessary steps to carry on the employer-of-record and staffing business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name clearance and NUANS search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada -- NUANS Name Search / ISED Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS search request with three proposed corporate names. Verify each name is distinctive, legally permitted, and usable in both English and French for Quebec. Confirm the selected name has no confusion with existing Canadian trademarks or corporate names. Retain the NUANS reservation for use in the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names in English and French
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or an earlier conflicting name appears, obtain a letter of no objection from the conflicting entity or amend the distinctive element and resubmit the NUANS search before filing the incorporation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal incorporation filing under the CBCA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form 4001 Articles of Incorporation through the Corporations Canada online portal. Set the authorized share structure and initial directors, confirm the registered office boundary in Quebec, state any restrictions on business, and electronically sign the submission. Pay the applicable registration fee and download the certificate of incorporation upon issuance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporations Canada issues a deficiency notice or objection, amend the articles in My Corporations Canada, provide the required corrected information within the stated deadline, and resubmit the affected pages for expedited review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Extra-provincial registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) -- Online Filing Service (CLIC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for registration of a federal legal person carrying on business in Quebec. Provide the Quebec establishment address, French version of the corporate name, head office address, list of directors and officers, and appointed attorney or representative for service if required. Pay the REQ registration fee and obtain the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and establishment record.
required_dossiers: Certificate of status from Corporations Canada
Quebec establishment and registered office address
Consent of attorney or representative for service in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ queries or rejects the registration, correct the record through the CLIC online service, provide a certified French translation of any non-compliant corporate document, and update the address or director data before resubmitting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board resolution, by-law adoption and share issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada -- initial directors return / REQ enterprise record update; board records lodged at registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or obtain the incorporator's written resolution. Approve the pro-forma First Board Resolution, adopt General By-law No. 1, approve the share subscription, issue share certificate number 1, and confirm officer appointments. File the initial directors return with Corporations Canada within 15 days and update the director and officer records with REQ.
required_dossiers: Share subscription letter and share certificate
Directors' and officers' consents and acceptances
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If either registry flags missing governance information, re-file the corrected return or REQ update, attach signed director declarations, and ensure all minutes, by-laws and shareholder records are held at the Quebec registered office for inspection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, payroll and CNESST employer account registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Revenu Quebec; Commission des normes, de l'equite, de la sante et de la securite du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a Business Number with the CRA and open the required program accounts: GST/HST, corporate income tax, and payroll source deductions. Register for Quebec sales tax (QST) with Revenu Quebec and obtain the employer number. Register the corporation with CNESST as an employer for workplace injury coverage and health and safety file purposes. Configure payroll direct debit rails and Wise for cross-border contractor payments.
required_dossiers: Directors' and officers' identification and social insurance numbers
Bank account verification or direct deposit enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA, Revenu Quebec or CNESST sends a notice of missing or incomplete data, respond through the respective online portal within the notice period, attach the requested corporate and director documents, and request retroactive effective dates where permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account opening and payment-rail configuration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian chartered bank or authorized financial institution; Wise Business
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present certified corporate records, the banking resolution, and directors' identification to open a Canadian dollar operating account and, if preferred, a US dollar account. Verify that the payroll account permits local payroll direct debit and that Wise can be linked for cross-border contractor disbursements. Complete the bank's know-your-client and beneficial ownership forms.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of certificate of incorporation
First board resolution authorizing bank accounts
Beneficial ownership and control information schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further AML/KYC material, provide the updated beneficial ownership schedule and proof of the Quebec registered office, or select a second Schedule I bank or credit union that accepts the corporate structure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Employment Placement Licensing Branch, acting with the Commission des normes, de l'equite, de la sante et de la securite du travail (CNESST)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Private Employment Agency Permit under the Act respecting private employment agencies, RLRQ c A-33.3; employer and temporary staffing registration under the Act respecting labour standards, RLRQ c N-1.1

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt -- Category 1 administrative/office occupancy; no threshold activity under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review, RLRQ c Q-2, r 11; no full EIA report required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office-only operations generate no process wastewater, VOCs or regulated air emissions; sanitary discharges flow to the municipal sewer system under applicable municipal by-laws; electronic waste, lighting and batteries are managed through RECYC-QUEBEC extended producer responsibility and municipal collection programs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal building occupancy permit issued by the local fire department confirming compliance with the Quebec Construction Code and Canadian Electrical Code for office occupancy; CNESST workplace safety clearance covering first-aid equipment and trained first-aider, fire prevention and evacuation plan, emergency exit inspection, hazard prevention program, and workers' compensation coverage for all employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenu Québec (provincial taxes) and Canada Revenue Agency (federal taxes), with online portals at https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/ and https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Register Canadian corporation in Quebec via Registre des entreprises du Québec. 2. Obtain Business Number (BN) from CRA via online portal or Form RC1. 3. Register for GST/QST and provincial corporate tax accounts with CRA and Revenu Québec if taxable supplies exceed threshold. 4. File annual corporate tax returns and remit taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; hybrid mismatch treatment governed by specific anti-avoidance rules under Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic filing of GST/HST and QST returns via CRA and Revenu Québec portals; digital record retention required; no real-time fiscal clearance or API stamping mandated for standard transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% GST/QST rate on exports to non-residents where services performed outside Canada; requires proof of export, non-resident recipient status, and foreign payment receipt for EOR staffing services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec audits; penalties up to 200% of tax plus interest; full retrospective clawback of zero-rated amounts with reassessment and fines for undocumented or fraudulent claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) and, for enforcement administration, the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) and FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; the Foreign Exchange Administration Function resides with the Department of Finance Canada and the Bank of Canada for monetary policy
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both capital and current accounts. There are no exchange controls under the Currency Act or the Bank of Canada Act restricting cross-border capital flows. Profit remittance by a Quebec business corporation is permitted without prior central bank approval; however, dividends, management fees, and intercompany payments must comply with transfer pricing rules under section 247 of the Income Tax Act and Quebec Revenue Agency reporting obligations. Payments to non-residents may be subject to withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, but no foreign exchange conversion certificate or approval is required. Foreign direct investment into Canada is reviewed only for net-benefit under the Investment Canada Act for enterprise value thresholds; an EOR staffing agency below the threshold is not subject to review.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement exists. Canada has no mandatory repatriation or forced conversion of export proceeds. Exporters may hold foreign currency accounts at Canadian financial institutions without reporting conversion. For goods exported, export declarations are filed via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) for statistical purposes; for services related to an EOR workforce, no foreign exchange conversion or surrender timeline applies. Billing in foreign currency is permitted, and the exporter may settle, hedge, or retain proceeds freely.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD and USD) for payroll, receivables, and disbursements
Operational Account + Capital Escrow / Trust Account where required for client funds
Operational Account and Treasury Management Account
Operational Co-operative Account for Quebec-based payroll and local clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low for core treasury dependency. Wise (formerly TransferWise) and Payoneer are licensed as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) under FINTRAC and the Quebec Autorité des marchés financiers when operating on a payments-only model, but they are not federally regulated banks under the Bank Act and cannot hold deposits in the same capacity as Schedule I banks. They may be used as supplementary payout rails, especially for cross-border contractor payroll to non-Canadian beneficiaries, provided funds are routed through a Canadian Schedule I bank settlement account. They cannot open an in-Canada demand deposit account naming the EOR entity, and payroll direct debits must clear through the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) operated by Payments Canada, which requires a Canadian bank membership.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandated for a business account in Quebec; however, all major Canadian banks require a designated signing officer or director to authenticate identity either in-branch or through a certified remote video KYC process using government-issued photo ID. In practice, for a Quebec incorporation a personal appearance by at least one director before a branch representative is often required for the first account, particularly if a credit facility or CDN dollar wire origination limit exceeding standard thresholds is requested. Remote opening is possible only where the entity is federally incorporated, the individual is a Canadian resident, and the bank offers an e-Signature plus Live Video interview protocol; non-resident directors or offshore shareholders will materially require an in-person visit to an authorized Canadian branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is non-resident or a foreign holding company in a low-tax jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certified corporate registry extract from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ); detailed UBO chain with passports; tax identification numbers in country of residence; source of funds documentation for initial capital; signed declaration of business purpose (EOR payroll administration); audited or reviewed financial statements of the parent entity; and legal opinion confirming no nominee shareholding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: High expected inbound wire flows from multiple foreign EOR clients in jurisdictions associated with shell-company abuse
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed Employer of Record service agreements listing end-client names; payroll register and beneficiary records; FINTRAC MSB registration if applicable; audited payroll liability schedule; paid-in capital evidence; and a written compliance manual verifying source-of-funds screening for every inbound wire above CAD 10,000.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Disproportionate cash withdrawals or demand for recurring distributions to offshore shareholders immediately after receiving payroll funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain three-way reconciliations of idle payroll escrow vs. operating funds; provide board resolution authorizing dividend/management-fee payments; evidence of arm's-length transfer pricing policy under Canada Revenue Agency interpretation; supporting tax clearance certificate from Revenu Québec; and a letter from a licensed Canadian CPA confirming that intercompany accounts are current.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Bank address mismatch or early registration of the corporation at a virtual-office address while the bank requires a physical Quebec location
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Obtain a permanent registered office in Quebec and a physical operational address; submit a lease agreement or sublease and utility bill; provide director's personal residential proof in Canada; attach REQ certificate of registration with attested address; and update the corporate minute book in advance of bank onboarding.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder equity injections from non-resident investors must be routed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 from an originating foreign bank to the Canadian bank's correspondent account with a detailed payment reference 'Contribution to capital under the Canada Business Corporations Act / Quebec Business Corporations Act' and the Canadian entity name. For cross-border equity capital of CAD 50,000 or more, the beneficial ownership and source-of-funds information must accompany the wire for FINTRAC large-value transaction reporting. Investment type must be coded for statistical purposes as 'O-Other Investment' or 'Direct Investment – Equity' under the Statistics Canada Balance of Payments reporting framework. All conversions to CAD may be executed at the receiving bank's spot rate; a Canadian withholding tax certificate may be required only for later distributions, not for the inward injection. The bank will also verify that the lender or shareholder is not a 'restricted entity' under the Investment Canada Act where the investment involves a cultural business; an EOR staffing agency is non-cultural and no net-benefit filing is required below the prescribed threshold.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Approved clearing rails include SWIFT MT103 for operational payments (supplier invoices, intercompany settlements, dividend distributions), SWIFT MT202 for correspondent-based transfers, Commercial LC (letters of credit issued by a Canadian Schedule I bank with MT700/MT710 messages) for international trade settlements, and domestic payments via Payments Canada ACSS (G3/G4 clearing files for payroll direct credits). For international contractor payroll, bulk cross-border payments are best executed through a Schedule I bank's international payment gateway using FX-Convert-and-Pay with same-day settlement to ISO 20022-compatible banks. EOR disbursements to contractors located outside Canada should be batch-processed under a standing instruction to the bank's foreign exchange desk, with each beneficiary receiving a separate MT103 containing the payroll reference and the employment contract identifier. Nondiscretionary statutory withholdings must be remitted on the general ledger and reported to Revenu Québec and CRA before funds leave Canada, regardless of the payment rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (CAD futures/forwards against USD, EUR, GBP) with a licensed Canadian Schedule I bank or authorized dealer
Cross-currency swaps (CAD against USD, EUR, GBP) for matching the EOR's inbound client billing currency and outbound payroll currency
FX options (European-style CAD calls/puts) purchased from a Canadian-registered investment dealer for risk premia protection

Composite hedging via dynamic spot splitting: converting a portion of inbound USD receipts through the DLR ETF physical swap or bank spot tickets, subject to the bank's leverage and mark-to-market margin requirements

Interest rate-linked cross-currency basis swaps offered under the Canadian Derivatives Rules (IIROC) by an approved derivatives dealer, provided the vehicle is a 'hedging purpose' transaction and not speculative under the EOR's written treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (CBCA or equivalent federal corporate registry return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for one consecutive year may lead to dissolution proceedings; late filing incurs administrative penalties and reinstatement costs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than the last day of the anniversary month of the initial registration in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers escalating late fees (CAD 50–200); continued non-filing may result in automatic dissolution and reactivation via legal proceeding.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No blanket statutory audit threshold for private business corporations in Quebec or under the CBCA unless the corporation is a reporting issuer (public), or qualifying shareholders holding at least 10% of shares request an audit; employment and payroll services do not automatically require audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for public/reporting issuers; private corporations may elect IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not require a standalone annual UBO filing; however, the REQ annual declaration must confirm directors and may require disclosure of controlling individuals. Federally incorporated corporations must maintain and, when applicable, annually confirm the Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register with Corporations Canada.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) / Beneficial Ownership (where applicable)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500-3,500 (for a small private EOR entity; higher if multi-jurisdictional payroll)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal statutory headline rate 15% general (after 13% General Rate Reduction) + Quebec 11.5% general = 26.5% combined general corporate income tax; Benefiting CCPCs: federal 9% + Quebec 3.2% = 12.2% combined on the first C$500K of active business income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD) reduces federal rate to 9% and Quebec rate to 3.2% on eligible active business income up to C$500,000 for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) — ineligible for a non-resident-parented EOR subsidiary unless resident-controlled; 13% General Rate Reduction for non-CCPC federally; Quebec offers the refundable tax credit for on-the-job training (up to 24% of eligible training expenditure capped per qualified trainee) relevant to staffing/EOR operations; no industry-conditional statutory tax holiday for EOR entities; C$500K SBD threshold is subject to business limit reduction where associated corporations exceed taxable capital C$15M.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return — filed electronically via CRA My Business Account / E-Services (T2 EFILE) or through a registered tax preparer; mandatory GIFI (Schedule 125) financial statements incorporated in the return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual regardless of business volume; a Quebec corporation with no income must still file T2
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after each fiscal year-end (e.g., a December 31 fiscal year-end is due June 30 of the following calendar year; if the due date falls on a weekend or statutory holiday, the filing deadline shifts to the next business day under CRA administrative practice). Payment deadline differs: balances are due 2 months after fiscal year-end (3 months for qualifying CCPCs), and instalments apply when net tax above C$3,000

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal corporate name, 9-digit Business Number (BN 'RT' tax account), provincial incorporation number, NAICS 2022 code 561330, fiscal period end date, and total worldwide gross revenue and total assets in box 100 fields to verify classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Canadian resident corporation’s identification; non-resident shareholders are not identified on the T2, but if any non-resident owns 10% or more of the shares or has control rights, cross-border leakages (Part XIII WHT and T106) will be triggered in the schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 1 – Line 360 (Net Income and Taxable Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting net income from the financial statements to taxable income: add-back of non-deductible expenses (fines, 50% meal/entertainment, punitive damages, non-arm’s length payments without adequate consideration) and deduction of tax items (capital cost allowance, losses, reserves).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an EOR owned by a non-resident group, treat intercompany charge/recharge income at arm’s length amounts only, or the adjustment becomes a s. 247(2) transfer-pricing adjustment; amounts paid to non-residents for management/administrative services that constitute 'management fees' are not deductible under s. 18(1)(b) ITA (and s. 92? no — QC equivalent) unless fully performed in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal Part I tax computation at the 38% statutory base rate, less 10% Federal Tax Abatement, less 13% General Rate Reduction (15% headline), or less 19% SBD reduction (9% headline) for eligible CCPC active business income; schedule yields net federal tax before credits and after investment tax credits; balance due computed on Schedule 400.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned Canadian corporation remains subject to Part I on Canadian-source business income and is not entitled to the SBD; use the 15% general rate line and preserve loss computations as prior-year non-capital losses carry-forward of up to 20 years; claim any Part XIII WHT credits on deemed dividends only if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims the federal SBD to lower the effective rate to 9% on up to C$500,000 of active business income (business limit) for CCPCs with aggregate taxable paid-up capital below C$15 million; requires active business carried on in Canada, not specified investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An EOR subsidiary controlled, directly or indirectly, by non-residents is a non-CCPC if it is not resident-controlled; in that case leave SBD claims blank. If the shares are held via a Canadian operating trust? Not necessary; SBD analysis should be validated by tax counsel before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 4 – Provincial/Territorial Allocation and Federal Abatement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocates taxable income between provinces/territories using the permanent establishment formula (sales and salaries weights) to compute the 10% federal abatement and provincial allocation; required for all multi-jurisdiction corporations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-parented EOR with only a Quebec permanent establishment will allocate 100% of taxable income to Quebec for the federal abatement; also mirrors the province of taxation for the federal 'surtax'? Not applicable; if no PE in Canada the Part I tax would be limited by treaty, but treaty relief is claimed outside the T2 via the treaty and Part XIII procedures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims refundable/non-refundable federal investment tax credits (SR&ED, apprenticeship credits, etc.) reducing Part I tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only bonuses with proper T2C? No — claim only if the EOR carried out qualifying work in Canada; credits generally not available to non-resident-owned corporations for passive or foreign-exported work; support with Form T661 for SR&ED.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory General Index of Financial Information (GIFI) schedules transmitting the balance sheet and income statement in standardized fields to CRA; reporting for payroll service revenue, contractor payouts, and commission expense.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report EOR gross service fees as revenue and contractor payroll disbursements as cost of sales (not employee salary) only if the payer truly is not the statutory employer under both CRA and Revenu Québec rules; any inconsistency with T4/NR4/T106 data will trigger audit matching.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of unpaid Part I tax plus 1% per full month of lateness (max 12 months); repeat failure within 3 years: 10% plus 2% per full month (max 20 months); interest at CRA prescribed rate plus 4% compounded daily runs from the balance-due date until payment; failure to file the T2 itself (zero balance) is penalized up to C$6,480 per return? As a summary: CRA also charges a minimum late-filing penalty based on tax owing and there are separate penalties per unfiled T4/NR4 information return under s. 162(6).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return — filed with Revenu Québec via CLICK electronic file-transmission system (mandatory electronic filing for corporations with gross revenue above the set threshold) or authorized professional filer
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual fiscal-period filing (mandatory even for a loss corporation)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 stub = June 30 due date; Revenu Québec applies the same 'next business day' practice as CRA only where expressly published). Quebec balance-due day: within 2 months of fiscal year-end (3 months for qualifying CCPC), with instalment rules coinciding with federal instalments

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), file number assigned by Revenu Québec, fiscal period end date, Business Number for the 'RQ' payroll account, and the mandatory check-off for the QST/QHSF accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent details are not filed on CO-17; disclose the parent/head office address in the accompanying schedules only when used for provincial attribution; failing to notify Revenu Québec of a change of Canadian-address for service is a compliance infraction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec accounting profit reconciled from financial statements: add-back of expenses not deductible under the Taxation Act (Quebec), including 50% of meals/entertainment, provincial fines, and any unremitted CNESST assessment penalties; deduction of Quebec-specific allowances (e.g., tax credits and the 3.2% small business deduction basis).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: EOR services recharged from the foreign parent: deduct only Quebec-performing service costs with contemporaneous supporting documentation; payments to non-arm's length non-residents must satisfy s. 447.2? of the Taxation Act (transfer-pricing standard) or the deduction is denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 Part 2 – Taxable income (revenu imposable, Line 108)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of Quebec taxable income after losses, reserves, and provincial adjustments; the Quebec portion of the federal 'provincial tax abatement' remains consistent with the permanent establishment allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An EOR with only a Quebec establishment uses 100% allocation; foreign-based operations must be excluded from provincial taxable income only if the intercompany arrangement has real Canadian substance — otherwise Quebec will assess the worldwide group service fee as unreasonable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 Part 3 – Income tax and credits (Lines 440-460)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec corporation income tax at 11.5% general rate (3.2% on eligible SBD income), less Quebec tax credits (e.g., refundable tax credit for on-the-job training, innovation credits) to yield net Quebec tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the 3.2% small business rate only where the corporation is a CCPC under the Taxation Act; a foreign-parent EOR non-CCPC is taxed at 11.5% on all active income, and Quebec Part IV tax on dividends received from subsidiaries is computed separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 Schedule CO-817 – Loss Carry-over / CO-772 Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec non-capital loss carry-forward (20 years) and carry-back (3 years) elections against taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Preserve Quebec loss records separately from federal losses; Quebec does not automatically align with federal adjustments, so a CRA TP adjustment must be separately processed with Revenu Québec within the 90-day/abatement window.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Employer payroll contribution computed on eligible Quebec remuneration (tier rates up to 4.26% for large payrolls) for the uninsured health fund; reported with the CO-17 even when no corporate income tax is payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For EOR models with global employees placed in Quebec, QHSF is levied on the Quebec payroll paid by the registered Quebec employer entity (or deemed employer); non-payment makes the compensation expense non-deductible and creates director exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Regional investment, innovation, and on-the-job training credit schedules; refundable credits attach to the return reducing tax payable or generating refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Training credit claims require each qualified trainee to be employed at a Quebec establishment of the taxpayer; cross-border contractors not on the Quebec payroll do not qualify.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid Quebec tax plus 1% per full month (max 12 months), and repeat-infraction 10% + 2% per full month (max 20 months); interest at the prescribed rate plus 4%; separate penalties apply to delay or omission of T4/RL-1 information slips (RL-1 for Quebec) at $25/day per slip to a maximum of $2,500 per corporation, escalating to $100/day per slip where the number of slips exceeds 100 (CRA, not RQ?), and for Quebec the equivalent under the Act respecting the ministère du Revenu.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% federal withholding under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (ITA) on dividends paid or deemed paid by a Canadian (Quebec) resident corporation to a non-resident of Canada; Quebec does not impose an additional separate dividend WHT because the federal Part XIII tax is levied uniformly and the benefit of the federal-provincial collection agreement applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain treaty-reduced withholding (e.g., 5%/15% dividends under Canada-US DTA; 10%/15% under Canada-China DTA): (1) the non-resident beneficial owner applies to the CRA on Form NR301 ('Application by a Non-Resident of Canada for a Reduction in the Amount of Non-Resident Tax Withheld') before or within 2 years after payment, attaching an official residence certificate from their home tax authority (TRC); (2) CRA reviews for beneficial ownership and issues an approval letter specifying the reduced rate and validity period; (3) the paying corporation withholds at the reduced rate only from the time it receives the CRA approval, otherwise it must withhold 25% and the non-resident applies for refund on Form NR7 (Application for Refund of Non-Resident Tax Withheld) — the refund route is also used where the treaty credit/disposition was not recognized at source; (4) Revenu Québec applies the same treaty determination for provincial WHT equivalents (e.g., on interest, royalties and management fees) and coordinates via the Joint Tax Treaty application with CRA; (5) the payer must retain all supporting documentation (residence certificates, shareholding vouchers, LOB declarations) for 6 years forensically? for audit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate is 25% for interest and royalties paid by a Canadian resident to a non-resident. Canada-US DTA relief: arm's-length interest is 0% (15% for related-party non-arm's length loans); royalties generally 10% with 0% for copyright royalties of literary, artistic or scientific works (software embedded in copyrighted work may qualify); Canada-China DTA: interest and royalties 10%. Management fees paid to non-residents (typical EOR parent recharges) carry no Part XIII exemption — 25% WHT if not structured as a proper arm's-length service fee; Quebec imposes its own supplemental WHT on interest, royalties and management fees paid to non-residents, but a foreign tax credit protocol and the Canada-Quebec collection agreement ensure no double-leakage at 25% twice.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: C$1,000,000 — Form T106 (Information Return on Transactions with Non-Residents) must be filed for a corporation's reportable non-arm's length transactions with non-resident related persons where the aggregate fair market value of specified transactions exceeds C$1,000,000 in the taxation year; a Group EOR platform must also file: Form RC4646 Country-by-Country Report where consolidated group revenue ≥ C$750,000,000; Quebec equivalent cross-border documentation regime under the Taxation Act (Revenu Québec TP documentation and CO-1066 filing threshold aligns with the federal C$1M aggregation methodology); contemporaneous TP documentation is expected for all reportable transactions and a full Local File is prudent for all intra-group services above C$100,000; whatever the threshold, CRA and Revenu Québec will disallow deductions on non-arm's length cross-border amounts whose pricing and documentation fail the s. 247(2) 'arm's length principle' — and a 10% TP gross-negligence penalty under ITA s. 247(3) applies to adjustment amounts.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Profit Split Method (e.g., transactional profit split and residual profit split)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not implement the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); however the substance-over-form principle is enforced through: (1) GAAR at ITA s. 245 (federal) and s. 1079.3 of the Quebec Taxation Act — an avoidance transaction lacking economic substance can be redrawn; (2) common-law corporate residency tests (central management and control), which determine whether the EOR's 'Canadian' entity truly manages operations in Canada; (3) treaty bilateral anti-abuse provisions (beneficial ownership, Limitation-on-Benefits where present and principal-purpose test per OECD Multilateral Instrument, which Canada has signed); and (4) CRA's criminal-level indicator analysis for 'shell payroll' arrangements. Accordingly the EOR's Canadian entity must maintain real commercial substance: own premises, Canadian-resident directors/officers, local payroll infrastructure, employment contracts and accounting records, or the entire arrangement is re-characterized as a PE or a disregarded conduit, exposing Part XIII WHT at 25% plus penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Payroll Trust Deviation / Unremitted Source Deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The EOR collects employee income tax, Canada Pension Plan (CPP/QPP), Employment Insurance (EI), Quebec Parental Insurance Plan (QPIP) and Health Services Fund (QHSF) contributions from wages but uses the withheld funds for corporate cash-flow rather than remitting them to CRA and Revenu Québec within statutory deadlines (generally 15th of the following month, with the monthly 3% deferred-remittance threshold). Even a single quarter of diversion creates an immediate statutory trust claim in favor of the Crown.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty under ITA s. 227(8)-(9): 10% penalty on the unremitted amount plus daily compound interest at the prescribed rate; second/subsequent failures within a relevant period attract 20%; CRA can issue a s. 227(16) direction freezing bank accounts, garnish receivables, and revoke the payroll 'RT' account; criminal prosecution for tax evasion under s. 239 ITA carries fines of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; the equivalent Quebec regime (Taxation Act and Act respecting the ministère du Revenu) adds provincial penalties of 12.5% to 25% plus surcharges for repeated misconduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director liability is automatic and severe: ITA s. 227.1 renders every director who was in office jointly and severally liable for the entire unremitted withholdings, penalties and interest regardless of fault or mental state; the Crown can assess directors personally, file judgments, seize personal assets, garnish director remuneration, and require travel clearance? on serious matters — no transactional travel clearance under CRA, but criminal arrest warrants effectively impose travel bans where evasion charges are laid; personal insolvency proceedings do not discharge this statutory trust debt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Worker Misclassification / Payroll Documentation Fraud (T4/RL-1/NR4 Manipulation)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: In an EOR/staffing model: classifying Quebec-based workers as foreign 'independent contractors' or offshore 'payroll vendors' to suppress CPP/EI/QPIP/QHSF and WSIB/CNESST obligations; issuing false T4 slips, omitting NR4 withholdings for non-resident employees, or failing to produce T106 schedules for the linked payroll chain. CRA's audit data-matching (payments, invoices, employment contracts) identifies misclassification quickly.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA determines an employer-employee relationship retroactively and assesses the full payroll deductions, employer penalties (10% of the unreported amounts under ITA s. 227(10)), worker-compensation back assessments by CNESST, unpaid vacation/social-benefit liabilities under the Quebec Act respecting labour standards, and late-filing penalties under ITA s. 162(6) (C$25/day per T4/NR4 slip up to C$2,500, C$100/day per slip where more than 100 slips are late, with a 4-year limitation window for reassessment).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the retroactively-assessed unremitted source deductions under ITA s. 227.1 and the Quebec equivalent, including interest and penalties; where the false classification was knowing (fraud were committed), directors face criminal personal prosecution under s. 239 ITA — imprisonment up to 5 years, criminal fines, civil restitution orders, and travel restrictions via criminal court undertakings.
